Subject: Request: 2-week extension + pricing for SKU add-on vs credit top-up

Hi Evelyn,

We're at the end of our 3-week pilot and the product team is asking for a short runway so they can finish the last two integration scenarios. Procurement also asked me to clarify pricing options so they can decide quickly:

- Option A: Add-on SKU for a 2-week runway (flat fee, simple PO)
- Option B: Credit top-up (pay-as-you-go, expires in 90 days)

Two asks from our side: can you confirm approximate cost for each option (we're a midsize provider, so ballpark numbers are fine) and whether any SLA or uptime commitments would change during the extension. Also, procurement prefers a DocuSign addendum rather than a manual amendment if possible.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call later this week if that helps.

Thanks,
Jessica Long
Director of Product Operations
BluePeak Health
jessica@bluepeakhealth.com

P.S. If you have a sample addendum or a quick breakdown, please send it over so I can circulate with procurement.

Subject: Re: Request: 2-week extension + pricing for SKU add-on vs credit top-up

Hi Jessica — thanks for the note and congrats to the team on reaching the finish line for the integration tests. Quick replies to your asks below.

High-level options we typically offer for short runway extensions:

1) SKU add-on (timeboxed extension) — flat fee that covers reserved capacity for the extension period. Easy for procurement (single PO), no change to model or API. Good if you want predictable latency.
2) Credit top-up — add token/embedding credits to the account. More flexible for bursty usage but credits expire (we normally do 90 days). Slightly more complex invoicing.

Rough ballpark (midsize health customer, estimated consumption from current pilot):
- SKU add-on, 2 weeks: $6,500 — reserved capacity, includes priority routing and standard support.
- Credit top-up (equivalent tokens): $5,000 — you get token credits, billed up front, expires in 90 days.

SLA: For hosted pilots we operate under our Pilot SLOs (best-effort with 99.5% historical availability). If you take the SKU add-on (reserved), we can extend a 99.9% SLO for the 2-week window and include a one-off credit mechanism for any system-level outages.

I'm looping in Marissa (pricing) to validate numbers and Priyom on the DocuSign/addendum. We can also prepare a short addendum PDF that procurement can sign.

If a call is easiest, I'm available Thu 7/16 9–11am ET or Fri 7/17 2–4pm ET.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales — Health & Life Sciences
Redwood Inference

T: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: 2-week extension + pricing for SKU add-on vs credit top-up

Hi Jessica — thanks for the details. I took Evelyn's ballpark and built two formal options you can take to procurement. I've attached a short addendum (Redwood_POC_Addendum_v2.pdf) and a one-page rate summary (ratecard-bluepeak.xlsx).

Option 1 — SKU add-on (recommended if you want consistent latency):
- 2-week reserved capacity SKU: $6,250 (we rounded down slightly to simplify the PO)
- Includes: priority routing, telemetry exports, and one dedicated on-call window with our platform engineer during the extension
- SLA for the SKU window: 99.9% uptime. Credit for downtime: pro-rated token credit for any sustained outage >30 minutes.

Option 2 — Credit top-up (flexible):
- $4,900 for token bucket (est. equivalent to current pilot usage)
- Credits expire in 90 days. No change to routing or priority.

Discounts & packaging notes:
- We can apply a 15% pilot-concession discount for BluePeak Health on either option (applies to this addendum only).
- If you commit to a 3-month Dedicated evaluation after the pilot, we'll ladder additional discounts into a formal offer.

Procurement stuff:
- Attached addendum is DocuSign-friendly and already references the BP-4721 deal id. Priyom, please flag any legal terms that need special attention (data retention, audit access).

Next steps:
- Jessica: pick Option 1 or 2 and whether you'd like the 15% concession applied.
- If Option 1 selected, we'll prepare a DocuSign addendum and an invoice for the PO.

Thanks — happy to take a quick call if you want to walk procurement through the addendum.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments:
- Redwood_POC_Addendum_v2.pdf (addendum template for a 2-week extension)

Jessica — we'll send the DocuSign envelope by EOD tomorrow. Procurement should be able to sign the addendum and return a PO number; please reply to this thread with the PO and the billing contact.
